testcase.name: signed-out and malformed identities cannot trigger backend account access
verified identity uses current server session and user before returning a minimal admin DTO
each request rechecks role and session rather than retaining cached admin privilege
only an active session belonging to this verified user and session can enter
expired or abandoned sessions are rejected even if a stale response says active
incomplete backend session data fails closed as unavailable
deleted provider records lose access and provider faults never expose raw errors
a stalled auth or provider lookup returns an unavailable result within its deadline
policy denials remain forbidden and do not grant access from unsafe metadata
missing server CSRF secret is an unavailable configuration, not an authorized session
page and request consumers preserve distinct 401, 403 and 503 failures
every engine mutation requires Clerk authority, exact origin and its current CSRF token
origin checking preserves normalized loopback requests and rejects host spoofing
bounded JSON and private sanitized failures remain available after password removal
legacy password endpoints return a retirement response without issuing or clearing sessions
legacy account command exits with Clerk instructions and no provisioning side effects
a revoked session with an unexpired JWT gets recovery, not a dashboard redirect loop
an anonymous browser gets the actual sign-in or sign-up form
a freshly verified admin can enter the dashboard
a verified ordinary account enters access pending without an admin redirect
provider verification failure renders a retry state with no auth widget or redirect
absent or malformed verified session identity cannot authorize an admin
only exact server-managed admin metadata grants access
banned, locked, disabled and malformed safety flags fail closed
missing user and mismatched backend identity cannot borrow another user's role
admin DTO exposes only bounded labels and the derived token
CSRF is stable in a session and isolated by session, user and secret
missing, short or malformed server secrets fail closed without echoing a secret
mutation token validation rejects omissions, tampering and a different session
only explicit endpoints and methods can reach the engine
engine origin cannot be a remote host, credential URL or arbitrary path
mutation bodies must be bounded JSON objects
dashboard hides upstream CSRF and rewrites only allowed report URLs
writes use a fresh server-side token and never forward browser credentials
report formats preserve downloads, masked text and protected nested links
stale reports, malformed upstream and outages fail without sensitive errors
uppercase UUID requests retain the report's canonical protected CSV link
